subject: Request: baseline per-1M token IO rates + supported models
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha@healthlink.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Baseline pricing request — 1M token IO split and model roster

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking a look. We're finalizing an internal vendor short-list for hosted inference and need a quick baseline from Redwood to compare to a few other providers. Two asks: 1) standard per-1M token IO pricing (separate input vs output rates) for your hosted API, and 2) the list of model variants you publish for each capability (chat/generation/embeddings) with any notable performance or latency notes.

We've attached a short RFP and a Q2 usage forecast to give scale context (pilot -> 3M tokens/mo; production could scale to 30M+). Any rough discounts for committed volume tiers or typical pilot credits would be useful but we're mainly after a simple IO rate table to put in our spreadsheet.

Thanks — can you get something back by EOD PST?

—Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of ML Platforms, HealthLink.ai
(samantha@healthlink.ai)

Attachment: HealthLink_RFP_v2.pdf (pdf, 312KB)
Attachment: usage_forecast_Q2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@healthlink.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Baseline pricing request — 1M token IO split and model roster

Hi Samantha — appreciate the context and the attachments. Short answers below; forwarding a compact rate table and model roster so you can drop into your comparison spreadsheet.

Quick baseline (hosted API, list pricing):
- Input tokens: $0.60 per 1,000,000 tokens ($0.0000006/token)
- Output tokens: $1.20 per 1,000,000 tokens ($0.0000012/token)
- Embeddings: $0.90 per 1,000,000 tokens (note: billed per embedding unit in some integrations)

Common model family availability (hosted):
- redwood-1-small (cost-optimized) — good for short prompts & classification; typical 50–200ms token latency for 512 contexts
- redwood-1-medium (balanced) — recommended for most chat/generation; higher quality with moderate latency
- redwood-1-xlarge (quality-first) — best for long-form generation; higher compute and latency
- redwood-embed-v2 — embeddings for semantic search & clustering (128/768-dim variants)

Notes on discounts & pilots:
- Standard self-serve rate above. For 3–10M tokens/mo we typically offer a pilot credit that covers the first month (ask-enabled case-by-case).
- Volume discounts start at committed monthly minimums (25M+ tokens/mo): tiered pricing and sustained-usage credits; typically 10–20% off list depending on contract length and support level.
- Dedicated/Private options (reserved capacity) have different economics and are priced separately — happy to introduce the solutions team if that looks relevant.

I'll attach a compact CSV of the above table and a short model-compatibility doc. If you want an explicit modeled estimate for your Q2 forecast, send the expected prompt/output ratios and avg tokens per request (or we can build one from your spreadsheet).

Next steps if you'd like to proceed:
1) We can run a 30-day pilot with X credits and help you instrument token reporting.
2) If pilot scales, we can introduce commercial terms and a committed-rate path — Marissa on CC handles commercial / discounts.

Hope this helps — happy to hop on a quick call if you'd prefer.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_baseline_rates.csv, model_roster_quick.pdf

From: Samantha Li <samantha@healthlink.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Roberto Gomez <rg@healthlink.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Baseline pricing request — 1M token IO split and model roster

Thanks Rishi — that's perfect and very helpful. Couple quick clarifications: 1) your table lists input/output per 1,000,000 tokens; can you confirm those are the billed IO units (not per 1K)? 2) for the 25M+ tier, is the 10–20% applied across both input and output rates or only output?

Also, do you typically enforce a minimum contract term for the deeper discounts (6/12 months)? For our evaluation we'll likely run a pilot then negotiate a short-term committed contract if the numbers look good.

If it's easier, we'd like a simple sample quote: 30M tokens/month committed for 6 months (apply volume discount and list the final per-1M IO rates). Can you return that by 5 PM PST?

—Samantha

On a separate note, any latency SLAs on hosted? We care more about 95th pct tail for interactive workflows.

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Baseline pricing request — 1M token IO split and model roster

Rishi — forwarding the HealthLink ask. They want a sample quote for 30M/mo committed x 6 months and clarity on the discount application. I drafted the quick math below; can you review and send final wording to Samantha? I'll approve standard commercial credit / discounting here but want to keep terms consistent with our policy.

Draft sample quote calculation (please confirm):
- List rates: Input $0.60 / 1M; Output $1.20 / 1M
- Proposed committed discount: 15% applied to both IO rates for 30M/mo (6-mo term)
- Final: Input $0.51 / 1M; Output $1.02 / 1M
- Pilot credit: $2,500 applied to first invoice if both parties sign a pilot SOW
- SLA note: hosted API provides 95th %-ile latency guidance per model in the console; SLA-backed latency commitments only on Dedicated or via attachable SLA addendum (available on enterprise deals).

If that looks right, respond and I'll finalize the commercial track and send the DocuSign path.

—Marissa
